newsitem.title: UK: POLL - Sterling seen firm until UK rate rises cease.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Sterling seen firm until UK rate rises cease.

text.p: Sterling is expected to cling to its dizzy heights for the next six months before finally slipping back to "fairer" values, currency experts polled by Reuters said on Thursday.
Likely interest rate rises in Britain would keep upward pressure on an already overvalued pound for the next three months, analysts said.
A median average from the poll saw sterling at 1.6325 dollars at the end of this month. By the end of October it could notch up to 1.6400, the median showed.
On August 4 and 5 Reuters asked 55 economists, currency strategists and traders in 20 financial centres to predict the level of cable, dollar/mark and dollar/yen one, three, six and 12 months ahead.
Reuters calculated the sterling/mark cross rate from these forecasts and found that the pound was set to remain above three marks for at least the next three months.
"The UK economy is still pretty buoyant itself and rising rates lend cable some support," said Keith Woodfin, currency analyst at FX Analytics in Connecticut.

"If you're looking for a high-yielding currency in one of the major industrialised countries, the best bet is to go with gilts and this also supports the pound, or prevents it from sliding too much lower." he added.
On August 5, sterling closed at 1.6237 dollars and 3.0563 marks, but it dropped around three cents and four pfennigs on Wednesday.

Economists are split as to whether British monetary authorities will announce a base rate rise from the current 6.75 percent later on Thursday, but even if they hold fire this time, the prospect of an increase later in the year would keep the pound buoyant.

"If there's a quarter point increase then sterling will remain firm. If rates don't go up now, then in a week or two people will start thinking of the next meeting in September," said Carlo Galazzi, deputy head of treasury sales at Nikko Bank in London.
But as threats of interest rate hikes dissipate, so will sterling's chances of further gains, analysts said.
The median average in the poll put sterling at 1.6000 dollars and 2.8193 marks in 12 months' time.
"When they (the monetary authorities) realise they've raised interest rates enough...then sterling will settle down and find its level. It's overdone at the moment," Galazzi said.
